name: Fix bugs
description: Reads your logs, finds the single root cause in your repository, proves the fix with a test, and opens a pull request. A person reviews; it never merges.

prompt.preamble: You read the logs, find the bug in the repository, and open a pull request that fixes it — or you stop and ask.

configurationSchema.description: What an installation supplies. Everything specific to your setup — which logs, which repository, which model — lives here; the agent itself knows none of it.

model.description: The model the reasoning loop runs on.

maxPathsPerRun.description: How many log findings one run may work. One is a good default: a run that opens one good pull request is a run that did its job.

maxTurnsPerPath.description: How many model turns one finding gets before the agent stops and asks. Twenty is enough to read, fix, test and open the pull request.

repository.description: The GitHub repository the agent fixes. Cloned into the run's container; the pull request targets it. Private or public makes no difference to the agent — only to what the token must be allowed to do.

baseBranch.description: The branch pull requests target. Protect it: the agent must never be able to push to it, and with branch protection on it cannot, whatever the model decides.

tokenKey.description: Secret name holding a GitHub token. It must be able to READ the repository (a private one needs this to clone at all), PUSH a branch to the repository — or to `pushTo`, if set — and OPEN pull requests against the repository. A fine-grained token scoped to contents:read+write and pull_requests:write on exactly these repositories is the right shape.

pushTo.description: Optional. A fork the agent pushes its fix branches to, when it may not push to `url` itself — the open-source contribution flow. The pull request is still opened against `url`, from the fork. Omit when the token can push branches to the repository directly.

logSources.description: Where the bugs come from: the logs. Each source is a command the harness runs (never the model) that prints the current FINDINGS as a JSON array — one row per distinct failure, not one row per log line. Rows: { id, title, count, firstSeen, lastSeen, samples }. `id` MUST be a stable signature of the failure (the same bug across runs yields the same id); the agent uses it to recognise a finding it has already opened a pull request for. `samples` are raw log entries, enough to locate the failure in code. What a 'distinct failure' is — grouping by exception + top frame, by route + status, by error code — is the source's decision, and the best place for it: it knows the log format, the agent does not.

examples.description: Unhandled errors from the production API over the last 24 hours, grouped by exception and top frame.

id.description: Short name for this source, e.g. worker-logs, sentry, ci-failures.

examples: Unhandled errors from the production API over the last 24 hours, grouped by exception and top frame.
description.description: What this source covers, in one line. Shown to the model with every finding.

command.description: The command, as an argv list, run from the repository root. Prints the JSON array on stdout. Any language; typically a script in your repository that queries your log store for the last window and groups the failures.

secrets.description: Secret names this command needs in its environment — a log-store API key, say. Handed to THIS command's invocation only; the model's shell never sees them.

review.description: The Human Eyes channel: where the agent's questions go for a person to answer. The pull request is the review of the FIX; this is the review of the agent's judgment calls along the way.

url.description: The machine-door URL of the Human Eyes board.

tokenKey.description: Secret name holding the board's agent token.

secrets.description: The UPPER_SNAKE names of every secret this installation resolves: the repository token, the review token, whatever the log sources need. Values live in the harness, never here.
